01.actor: The Sages of Kafrei and Rav
01.event: The Sages reversed the names of Shmuel's and Karna's opinions and sent the question to Rav.
01.turn: Rav, tested with the names swapped, reacted with an oath.
01.outcome: Rav swore that she needs both a bill of divorce and refusal, and that Shmuel could never have said otherwise.
01.summary: After Shmuel and Karna disagreed about a minor betrothed without her father's consent, the Sages sent the question to Rav with the two opinions' attributions swapped. Rav swore by God that she needs both a divorce and refusal, and said Shmuel would never say such a thing.
01.missing: The framing of the question is in [3]; the passage opens mid-exchange and the reason for the swap is only implied.

02.event: Ulla visited Pumbedita, saw Rav Yehuda's grown son unmarried, and asked why.
02.turn: Ulla argued that nobody can be sure their own lineage is unflawed, citing verses and Rabbi Abbahu's reading of them.
02.outcome: Rav Yehuda asked what to do, and Ulla told him to go after the silence, the Western test of who stays silent in a quarrel.
02.summary: Ulla visited Rav Yehuda in Pumbedita and noticed his adult son was unmarried. Rav Yehuda said he did not know where to find a woman of sound lineage. Ulla replied that no one can be sure of their own descent, and after verses about the ravished women of Zion were discussed, Rav Yehuda asked what to do. Ulla told him to follow the silence, as in the West, where the person who falls silent first in a quarrel is deemed better born.

03.actor: A man who sold his property
03.event: He sold his property in order to go up to Eretz Yisrael, went up, but could not settle there.
03.turn: Having gone but not settled, he tried to cancel the sale.
03.outcome: Rava ruled in one version that he may cancel, and in another that he may not, since he did go up.
03.summary: A man sold his property intending to go up to Eretz Yisrael and told the buyer so. He went up but was unable to settle there, and wanted the sale undone. Rava is reported as ruling he can cancel because people go up to settle, or, in the other version, that he cannot because he did what he intended and went up.

04.actor: Reish Lakish, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yohanan
04.event: A man who claimed another was a priest because he read first in the synagogue was challenged by Reish Lakish, who wanted proof of teruma at the threshing floor.
04.turn: Rabbi Elazar objected that priesthood does not cease where there is no threshing floor; later Rabbi Yohanan said the same, showing it was his teaching.
04.outcome: Reish Lakish glared at Rabbi Elazar and reproached him for not citing Rabbi Yohanan in his name.
04.summary: A man testified before Reish Lakish that someone was a priest because he read first in the synagogue. Reish Lakish asked if he had seen him receive a share at the threshing floor, and Rabbi Elazar replied that priesthood does not vanish where there is no threshing floor. Later a similar case came before Rabbi Yohanan, who made the same reply. Reish Lakish then rebuked Rabbi Elazar for hiding that it was Rabbi Yohanan's teaching.

05.actor: A man testifying before Reish Lakish; Rabbi Elazar
05.event: A man claimed another was a priest because he read first, and Reish Lakish asked about the threshing floor.
05.turn: Rabbi Elazar objected that priesthood does not lapse without a threshing floor.
05.summary: A man told Reish Lakish that someone was a priest because he had read first in the synagogue. Reish Lakish asked whether he had seen him receive a share at the threshing floor. Rabbi Elazar objected that priesthood does not lapse where there is no threshing floor.
05.missing: The passage ends at the objection; the sequel in [5] is outside it.

06.actor: A depositor, Rav Dimi's household and Rabbi Abba
06.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without saying anything, and the claimant came before Rabbi Abba.
06.turn: Rav Dimi's household had no instructions, so the claim had to be judged.
06.outcome: Rabbi Abba awarded it to the claimant because Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the man gave a distinguishing mark, with the proviso that this fails if he habitually enters the house.
06.summary: A man left silk in Rav Dimi's house, and Rav Dimi died without saying whose it was. The claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who ruled for him, since Rav Dimi was known not to be wealthy and the claimant described the silk. He added that this works only if the claimant does not habitually go in and out there.

07.event: Neighbors asked a gentile superintendent to rent them his domain so they could carry on Shabbat, and he refused.
07.turn: They asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent from his wife instead.
07.outcome: Rabbi Zeira ruled that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge, so they could.
07.summary: A gentile superintendent in Rabbi Zeira's neighborhood refused to rent his domain to his neighbors for an eiruv. They asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent from his wife. He answered, citing Reish Lakish in the name of Rabbi Hanina, that a wife may establish an eiruv without her husband's knowledge.

08.event: Ravina held wine of his orphaned nephew and was taking his own wine to Sikhra, and asked Rav Ashi whether he could take the orphan's wine along.
08.turn: He needed permission to sell the orphan's wine that way.
08.outcome: Rav Ashi told him to go, since the orphan's wine was no better than his own.
08.summary: Ravina was guarding wine belonging to his orphan nephew and was about to take his own wine to Sikhra to sell. He asked Rav Ashi whether he could bring the orphan's wine too. Rav Ashi said yes, since the orphan's wine was no better than his.

09.actor: King Yannai, Elazar ben Po'ira and the Sages
09.event: Yannai held a feast for the Sages after a victory, and the scoffer Elazar ben Po'ira persuaded him that the Pharisees resented him.
09.turn: Yannai had the Pharisees tested, Yehuda ben Gedidya told him to give up the priesthood, and Elazar pressed him to kill the Sages.
09.outcome: Yannai had the Sages killed, the world was desolate of Torah until Shimon ben Shatah restored it.
09.summary: After conquering sixty cities, King Yannai feasted the Sages. The scoffer Elazar ben Po'ira told him the Pharisees resented him, and when Yehuda ben Gedidya told Yannai to leave the priesthood to Aaron's descendants, Elazar urged him to crush the Sages. Yannai complied, the Sages were killed, and the world was desolate of Torah until Shimon ben Shatah restored it.

10.actor: Rabbi Hanina, his wife and a pauper
10.event: Rabbi Hanina sent a weekly sum to a pauper by his wife, who overheard the pauper being asked what kind of tablecloths he dines on.
10.turn: His wife reported that the man did not need charity.
10.outcome: Rabbi Hanina said we should be grateful to swindlers, because without them we would sin daily by neglecting the truly poor.
10.summary: Rabbi Hanina regularly sent four dinars to a pauper before Shabbat. Once his wife brought it and returned saying the man did not need it, since she heard him asked whether he dined on silver or gold tablecloths. Rabbi Hanina replied that we should be grateful to swindlers, since they give us an excuse for any failure to help the truly poor.

12.event: A man willed his daughter a palm tree and died leaving two halves of palm trees, which the heirs wanted to give her.
12.turn: Rav Ashi doubted whether people call two halves a palm tree.
12.outcome: Rav Mordekhai told him Rava said that people do, so the heirs may give her the two halves.
12.summary: A man left his daughter a palm tree and died owning only two halves of trees. The heirs wanted to give her the halves. Rav Ashi wondered whether people call two halves a palm tree, and Rav Mordekhai reported in Rava's name that they do, so the heirs can satisfy the bequest this way.

13.actor: A depositor, Rav Dimi's household and Rabbi Abba
13.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without saying anything, and the claimant came before Rabbi Abba.
13.turn: Rav Dimi's household had no instructions, so the claim had to be judged.
13.outcome: Rabbi Abba awarded it to the claimant because Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the man gave a distinguishing mark, with the proviso that this fails if he habitually enters the house.
13.summary: A man left silk in Rav Dimi's house, and Rav Dimi died without saying whose it was. The claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who ruled for him, since Rav Dimi was known not to be wealthy and the claimant described the silk. He added that this works only if the claimant does not habitually go in and out there.

14.actor: A blind man, Mar Shmuel and a messenger
14.event: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Shmuel was late, and Shmuel's messenger missed him on the road and then reported to Shmuel that the man's wife had committed adultery.
14.turn: The blind man came to Shmuel to ask whether to heed that report.
14.outcome: Shmuel told him that if he trusted the messenger he should divorce her, and otherwise not.
14.summary: A blind man who studied mishnayot before Shmuel was late one day, so Shmuel sent a messenger after him. They took different roads and missed each other, and the messenger went to the man's house and returned saying his wife had committed adultery. The blind man asked Shmuel what to do, and Shmuel said to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not otherwise.

15.event: Rav Yehuda, nearly blind, struggled to read and sign documents himself, and Ulla told him he need not.
15.turn: Ulla pointed to Rabbi Elazar and Rav Nahman, who had court scribes read documents to them.
15.outcome: The outcome is not given beyond Ulla's advice and a limit on when it applies.
15.summary: Rav Yehuda, barely able to read, struggled to read and sign documents. Ulla told him this was unnecessary, since Rabbi Elazar and Rav Nahman had scribes read documents to them and then signed.
15.missing: Whether Rav Yehuda followed the advice is not stated; the passage mostly turns into a rule about when scribes may read.

16.event: Ravina examined a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia in his teacher Rav Ashi's lifetime, and Rav Ashi asked why he did so.
16.turn: Ravina cited Rav Hamnuna, Rav Ashi said that tradition says he did not rule, and Ravina answered that he did rule for Rav Hisda, his colleague-teacher, as Ravina was for Rav Ashi.
16.outcome: Ravina argued that he was a disciple-colleague, but Rav Ashi's response is not shown.
16.summary: Ravina examined a knife for slaughtering while his teacher Rav Ashi lived in the same country, and Rav Ashi asked why. Ravina cited Rav Hamnuna ruling in another town in Rav Hisda's lifetime. Rav Ashi said that report was that he did not rule, and Ravina replied that both reports are true, because Hamnuna ruled for Rav Hisda as a colleague, and Ravina was likewise Rav Ashi's disciple and colleague.
16.missing: Rav Ashi's final verdict on Ravina's conduct is not shown.

18.actor: Rav Yosef son of Rava, and his father
18.event: Rava sent his son Rav Yosef to study six years before Rav Yosef, but at three years, on the eve of Yom Kippur, the son wanted to visit his wife.
18.turn: His father heard, took a weapon, went to meet him and rebuked him.
18.outcome: The quarrel left both too preoccupied to eat the pre-fast meal.
18.summary: Rava sent his son Rav Yosef to study for six years. Three years in, on the eve of Yom Kippur, the son said he would go see his household. His father heard, took a weapon and went to meet him, rebuking him for remembering his wife. The argument was so consuming that neither ate the pre-fast meal.

19.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a ruling, and Abaye said he himself had taught it.
19.turn: Abaye reminded him of the discussion in which he explained the mishna in Rav's name.
19.outcome: The ruling is restored through Abaye's reminder.
19.summary: Rav Yosef, whose illness made him forget his studies, said he had not heard a certain teaching. Abaye reminded him that he had taught it, citing the brothers eating at their father's table, and Rav's explanation that the mishna concerned brothers receiving a portion.
19.missing: The exchange is mainly a recitation of a legal teaching; there is barely an event and no stated ending.

20.actor: Shmuel, Rav Dimi bar Yosef and a divorcee
20.event: A divorced woman came before Shmuel, who sent Rav Dimi bar Yosef to test whether her baby recognized her.
20.turn: Rav Dimi put her among other women and carried the child past them, and the child looked at her joyfully while she looked away.
20.outcome: Rav Dimi told her to lift her eyes and take her son, since the child recognized her.
20.summary: A divorcee came before Shmuel and he had Rav Dimi bar Yosef test whether her child recognized her. Rav Dimi put her among a row of women and carried the baby past them. When it reached her, the baby looked at her face happily while she turned away, and Rav Dimi told her to lift her eyes and take her son.
